subject.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens

question: Should the refreshed PR preserve MCP/LSP runtime selector tokens in inherited spawned-session allowlists after filtering them through the same effective policy layers as concrete tools?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and the PR is a narrow candidate fix, but the exact merge result touches child-session authorization and is currently conflicting with newer policy code.

options.title: Refresh And Review Policy Parity
options.body: Resolve the conflicts, preserve declared allowlist and cron policy-capture behavior from current main, and have an agent/gateway owner confirm the selector-filtering policy intersection before merge.

options.title: Accept Security Boundary Risk After Refresh
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally land the refreshed branch if they judge the supplied tests and real proof cover child-session authorization well enough.

options.title: Replace Near Runtime Materialization
options.body: If owner review finds inherited selector preservation is the wrong boundary, pause this branch and replace it with a narrower owner-authored fix closer to MCP/LSP materialization.

recommendation.title: Refresh And Review Policy Parity
recommendation.body: Resolve the conflicts, preserve declared allowlist and cron policy-capture behavior from current main, and have an agent/gateway owner confirm the selector-filtering policy intersection before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the inherited restriction propagation path that the PR is repairing, so they are the best history-backed owner for the boundary choice.
